procedural_history.originating_court: Vimantal Police Station, Nanded (Crime No. 104 of 2013)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 04.07.2016 of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Aurangabad Bench at Aurangabad in Criminal Writ Petition No. 39 of 2015.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court directed payment to the petitioners and ordered that the amount be recovered from the Investigating Officer/in-charge at the relevant time in Crime No.104 of 2013, Vimantal Police Station, Nanded. The State was also ordered to pay costs of the petition to the petitioners.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Investigating Officer-In-Charge appealed against the High Court's direction, contending that the appellant ought not to have been directed to make over the payment unless and until the liability or responsibility is fixed. The Supreme Court disposed of the appeal.

issue.issue_text: Whether the State can be directed to recover the compensation amount for a custodial death from the Investigating Officer-in-Charge before their liability for the crime is formally established.

facts: The family of a man named Pravin, who died in police custody, filed a writ petition in the High Court.
The High Court ordered the State to pay Rs. 7 lakhs in compensation to the family.
The High Court also directed the State to recover this compensation amount from the Investigating Officer-in-Charge involved in the case.

The Investigating Officer appealed this specific direction, arguing that the recovery order was improper because his personal liability or responsibility for the death had not yet been formally established.
law: The Supreme Court acknowledged the established legal principle that the State is vicariously and strictly liable for the infringement of fundamental rights, such as the right to life, by its public servants.
In cases of custodial death, the State has a duty to pay compensation to the victim's family.
While the State is primarily liable to pay the compensation, it has the right to be indemnified by the wrongdoer, meaning it can recover the amount from the specific officials found to be at fault.
application: The Court considered the Investigating Officer's argument that it was unfair to order recovery from him before his guilt was proven.
The Court noted that legal proceedings to determine who was liable for the custodial death were still pending.
The Supreme Court reasoned that ordering the recovery of the compensation amount from the officer before his liability was formally determined in those pending proceedings was premature.
The Court balanced the State's right to recover the money with the officer's right not to be penalized until his fault was legally established.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court modified the High Court's order. It ruled that the State must first pay the compensation to the victim's family, but it can only recover that amount from the erring officials *after* their liability for the crime has been formally established ('fastened') in the appropriate legal proceedings.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the State can be directed to recover the compensation amount for a custodial death from the Investigating Officer-in-Charge before their liability for the crime is formally established.
appellant_arguments: The compensation amount should not be recovered from the Investigating Officer-in-Charge unless and until their liability or responsibility for the death is formally fixed and established.
respondent_arguments: The State acknowledged that proceedings were pending in which the question of liability for the death would be determined.

cases.case_name: Delhi Airtech Services Private Limited and Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr.
cases.principle: In a case of default by officials, costs can be imposed which are to be deposited at the first instance by the State, and then recovered from the salaries of the defaulting/erring officers.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The State may recover the amount of compensation from erring officials only after the liability for the crime in question is fastened upon them.
obiter: In a case dealing with default on part of the officials in depositing the amount in terms of the Land Acquisition Act, the claimants would be entitled to costs which shall be deposited at the first instance by the State Government and then would be recovered from the salaries of the defaulting/erring officers/officials in accordance with law.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court modified the High Court's direction, ruling that the State is only at liberty to recover the compensation amount for a custodial death from the concerned officials after their liability for the crime in question has been formally established or "fastened." The recovery cannot precede the determination of guilt.
legal_tests_applied: The principle of State liability for infringement of fundamental rights by public servants, where the State pays compensation first and then has the right to be indemnified by the specific wrongdoer once their liability is established. (D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal)

The precedent that recovery from erring officials must be done "in accordance with law," which implies that a formal inquiry or legal process to determine fault must be completed before recovery can be initiated. (Delhi Airtech Services Private Limited and Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr.)
why_appellant_lost: The appellant did not lose; the court accepted their argument and modified the High Court's order in their favor.
why_respondent_won: The respondent (the original petitioner/victim's family) won in the sense that the State's primary liability to pay compensation was not overturned. The State, as a co-respondent, won by having its right to eventually recover the compensation from the liable officials explicitly affirmed, albeit with a crucial clarification on the timing of such recovery.
policy_considerations: It is contrary to the principles of justice to impose a financial penalty on an officer by recovering a compensation amount from them before their liability or responsibility for the underlying crime has been formally and legally established.
